subject: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finosys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for your patience as we finished our internal review. Attached are three artifacts we promised: a short-form CSV timeline (incident-timeline-20270427.csv), an executive PDF postmortem (postmortem-summary-20270427.pdf), and a sampled logs bundle for your SREs (forensics-sample-logs-20270427.tar.gz).

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a race condition in the KV-cache invalidation path that allowed stale keys to return after a partial disk-to-GPU reconciliation failure.
- Impact window: 2027-04-23T22:13 — 2027-04-24T01:07 UTC.
- Visible impact: elevated token latency and ~0.6% token duplication for affected sessions.

What we did for you:
- Immediate mitigation (completed during incident): rolled back a recent rollout, hot-fixed the reconciler, and forced a full KV cache flush for affected pools.
- Post-incident: completed code fix, added end-to-end regression tests, and integrated a new reconciliation validation step.

Action items and owners (short):
- Provide Finosys with a sanitized log subset and replay instructions — Marcus (done, attached).
- Add synthetic workload to replicate the failure mode in QA — Dylan (ETA 2027-05-05).
- Increase telemetry alerting for KV reconciliation anomalies — Neha (ETA 2027-04-30).

If you want a 30-minute walk-through of the artifacts and validation steps, I can set aside time tomorrow morning PST. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and whether your team needs additional evidence or a longer technical readout.

Apologies for the disruption — we own this and will verify it does not recur.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline-20270427.csv, postmortem-summary-20270427.pdf, forensics-sample-logs-20270427.tar.gz
From: Elena Morales <elena@finosys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments

Marcus —

Received, thanks. Quick q: the timeline shows two handoffs around 22:45 UTC; can you confirm which internal job triggered the reconciler during that window? Our ops saw token duplication starting ~22:16 UTC.

Also, we will want a replayable packet for our on-call to validate the fix in a staging replica before you do the production rollout. Is the sampled logs tar safe to replay in our environment or do you recommend we use a sanitized replay script?

Elena
SRE Lead, Finosys
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finosys.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments

Elena —

Short answers:
- The reconciler job was triggered by a backfill process that started a full pool sync; there was a race between the backfill and a streaming KV flush. The timeline CSV has the exact goroutine traces around 22:44 — I highlighted the two handoff events in rows 68–73.
- The sampled logs are safe for replay in a staging replica, but they contain internal IPs and temporary tokens. Use the sanitized replay script I attached in the Drive link (see related_links) — it replaces tokens and collapses internal IPs. If you prefer, we can produce a replay-only payload that strips more metadata; say the word and we'll generate it.

Dylan — can you add the replication steps for Elena's SRE team (short checklist) and confirm ETA for the QA synthetic?

Marcus
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@finosys.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments

Elena / Marcus —

Checklist for Finosys SRE replay (short):
1) Stand up a staging pool with the same sequence length distribution and enable prefix-KV mode.
2) Place the sanitized logs bundle in /opt/replay and run ./replay.sh --timestamps --collapse-internal.
3) Watch for: duplicate token emission (marker: token_seq++ without KV refresh) and elevated latency > 300ms.
4) After replay, run the reconciler validation tool: ./kvcheck --validate --sample 1000.

I will push a replay-only payload (no IPs/tokens) by EOD and the synthetic workload to our QA cluster by 2027-05-05. Neha will add the alert rule for reconciliation anomalies before EOD 2027-04-30.

—Dylan
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident timeline, evidence ledger, and owner commitments

Thanks all — Elena, Dylan will upload the replay-only payload to the Drive and I'll email you the access link as soon as it's available.

A couple of additional commitments for transparency:
- We will run a coordinated staged rollout of the reconciler fix with Finosys participation and a two-hour canary window.
- We will share regression test results and a short validation report within 48 hours of the staged rollout.
- We will include Finosys on the post-rollout verification call and keep a joint incident channel open for 72 hours.

If that plan looks good, please reply to confirm and tell us which timezone window you prefer for the staged rollout (we propose 2027-05-07 00:00–04:00 UTC as our first option).

Marcus
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
